subject.title: fix(reef): bound JSONL store file reads to prevent OOM on oversized audit/replay stores

question: Should an oversized Reef replay ledger remain unavailable until an operator performs an explicit recovery, or should OpenClaw define and implement a lossless bounded compaction/migration contract?
rationale: This choice determines the receipt-reuse security invariant and the persistent-data recovery contract; an automated repair cannot safely choose retention semantics for records outside the cap.

options.title: Fail closed and add operator recovery guidance
options.body: Restore the fail-closed replay-ledger error and document a bounded operator recovery path that cannot silently discard receipt records.

options.title: Design lossless compaction first
options.body: Keep the PR paused until a maintainer-approved design can compact or migrate the entire ledger without exceeding memory bounds or dropping records.

options.title: Accept bounded-prefix deletion
options.body: Accept that completed receipts beyond the cap may be forgotten and document the resulting replay-security tradeoff explicitly.

recommendation.title: Fail closed and add operator recovery guidance
recommendation.body: Restore the fail-closed replay-ledger error and document a bounded operator recovery path that cannot silently discard receipt records.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main Reef protocol ownership could not be established without the required repository-history inspection.
